# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_005_page_001.jpg

---

**5:1** Then the righteous will stand with great confidence before those who have oppressed them and treated their labors with contempt.

**5:2** When the wicked see him, they will be struck with terrible fear, and they will be overwhelmed at the unexpected nature of his salvation.

**5:3** They will speak to one another in remorse, and in anguish of spirit they will groan, and say:

**5:4** "This is the man we once held up to ridicule and made a byword of reproach — we fools! We counted his life a form of madness, and his end without honor.

**5:5** How has he come to be numbered among the sons of God? And how is his lot cast among the holy ones?

**5:6** So it was we who strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine upon us, and the sun did not rise for us.

**5:7** We wore ourselves out on paths of lawlessness and destruction, making our way through trackless wastes; but the way of the Lord we never came to know.

**5:8** What has our pride profited us? And what benefit have we gained from our boasted wealth?

**5:9** All those things have passed away like a shadow, like a rumor that runs quickly by —

**5:10** like a ship that passes through the surging sea, of which, when it has gone past, no track can be found, no path of its keel in the waves;

**5:11** or as when a bird flies through the air, no sign of its passage is found: the light air, beaten by the strokes of its wings and divided by the force of its rushing flight, is traversed, and afterward there is no evidence that it ever passed through;

**5:12** or as when an arrow is shot at its mark — the air that was struck closes up at once and the arrow's path is impossible to trace.

**5:13** So we too, when we were born, ceased almost immediately to exist, and of virtue we had not a single sign to show, but we were consumed in our own wickedness."

**5:14** For the hope of the ungodly is like chaff driven away by the wind, and like thin frost scattered by a storm; it disperses like smoke before the wind and passes like the memory of a visitor who stayed for only a day.

**5:15** But the righteous live for ever; their reward is with the Lord, and the Most High watches over them.

**5:16** Therefore they will receive from the hand of the Lord a glorious crown and a beautiful diadem; for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his arm he will shield them.

**5:17** He will take his zeal as his full armor, and will arm all creation to punish his enemies;

**5:18** he will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and put impartial justice on as a helmet;

**5:19** he will take holiness as an invincible shield,

**5:20** and whet his relentless anger as a sword; and creation will marshal itself with him to fight against the reckless.

**5:21** Bolts of lightning will fly from true aim, leaping to their target from the clouds as if from a taut bow,

**5:22** and hailstones full of wrath will be hurled from a catapult; the waters of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will close over them without mercy;

**5:23** a mighty wind will arise against them, and like a tempest it will blow them away. Lawlessness will devastate the whole earth, and wrongdoing will topple the thrones of the powerful.

---

*LOGOS notes: The divine armor passage (vv. 17–20) is a direct source for the Pauline "armor of God" (Eph 6:13–17). The three ship/bird/arrow similes (vv. 10–12) form a rhetorical triad demonstrating that the ungodly leave no trace. "Chaff" at v. 14 (EMET "thistledown") — achuron is grain chaff, not thistledown; LOGOS corrects.*
